forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Dorset Council expects £145m government grant covering 90% of its £148.7m schools deficit
news_drafts.lead:
Dorset Council expects to receive about £145m from government on 30 November 2026 towards its cumulative dedicated schools grant (DSG) deficit, the overspend on the government grant that funds schools, which stood at £148.7m at 31 March 2026. The government accepted the council's SEND reform plan, and the grant is equivalent to 90% of that deficit. The council's external auditor, in its annual report, says support beyond 2025/26 remains uncertain and depends on the level and duration of government funding.

The deficit rose from £95.6m to £148.7m during 2025/26, driven primarily by a £55.2m overspend in high needs, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The council's cabinet was told the 2026/27 DSG overspend is forecast at £74.3m, with the cumulative deficit forecast at approximately £150m by 31 March 2028. Education, health and care plans have risen to around 5,000 from 1,407 in 2013. The balance of £3.7m is to come from the council's Safety Valve reserve.

The council has set up a £17.5m DSG Recovery Reserve. It estimates its total contribution to March 2028 at £18.8m, assuming 90% grant funding each year to 2027/28, leaving a forecast gap of £1.3m. The auditor says the reserves appear sufficient for that gap. Separately, Dorset Travel is projecting a £1.752m underspend, with SEND transport contracts for September 2026 assessed at circa £2.2m below budget.

news_drafts.headline: Dorset Council expects £145m high needs grant in November; schools deficit was £148.7m in March
news_drafts.lead:
Dorset Council expects a £145m High Needs Stability Grant from government in November, after its Reform Plan for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) was accepted in October 2026. Its cumulative deficit on the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, was £148.7m at 31 March 2026. The grant is forecast to overspend by £74.3m in 2026/27.

The Cabinet finance report calls acceptance of the plan a key milestone in securing a 90% write-off of the cumulative overspend. The £145m leaves a balance of £3.7m, to be funded from the reserve set up to support the Safety Valve programme. The medium-term financial plan report says the projections show the deficit returning to around £150m at 31 March 2028, when the statutory override, the government rule that keeps the deficit off the council's main balance sheet, ceases. The finance report says the override was extended from March 2026 to March 2028, and puts the carrying cost of the deficit at circa £6m in interest foregone.

The same report forecasts SEND transport spending at £22.3m for 2026/27, up 10% from £20.2m in 2025/26. It says 2025/26 had the lowest increase in recent history, which it attributes to market stability and efficiency work by Dorset Travel. Contract changes from September 2026 have been assessed as circa £2.2m below budget for SEND transport and circa £0.5m below budget for mainstream school transport.

news_drafts.headline: Dorset Council forecasts a £74.3m schools grant overspend for 2026/27, within high needs
news_drafts.lead:
Dorset Council forecasts a £74.315m overspend on its dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools, for 2026/27, according to papers for the Schools' Forum meeting on 6 November. The forecast, made at 30 September 2026, sits in the high needs block, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). The council budgeted for an in-year deficit of £73.328m.

The paper attributes the main pressure to growth in SEND demand and in the number of children with an education, health and care plan. The cumulative deficit was £148.7m at 31 March 2026. The council expects a £145m High Needs Stability Grant in November 2026, after its SEND Reform Plan was accepted in October, which brings the forecast cumulative deficit at March 2027 to £76.719m. The deficit is forecast at about £150m by 31 March 2028. The paper says the council has access to £148.7m less cash than it would otherwise, at a cost of circa £6m in interest foregone. A statutory override, a temporary government rule that keeps the deficit off the council's main balance sheet, was extended from March 2026 to March 2028 in June 2025.

The forum also has a plan to commission 2,056 specialist places for September 2027, committing £17.9m of the high needs block: 996 in special schools, 397 in learning centres, 370 in further education colleges and 293 in Specialist Inclusion Bases. The paper says this will be funded from the block in 2027-28 and 2028-29.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 9 - Auditor’s Annual Report year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Dorset selected Local Pensions Partnership Investments as its new pooling partner after the Government's consolidation decision for Brunel.
findings.detail: The auditor notes that the Government decided Brunel should consolidate with another pool. The Council approved governance arrangements to support the transition to LPPI.
findings.matters: Pool changes forced by the Government's consolidation decision affect every LGPS fund in a pool, so peers will watch the transition.
findings.quote: Dorset selected Local Pensions Partnership Investments (LPPI) as its new pooling partner

findings.paper_title: Appendix 9 - Auditor’s Annual Report year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Pension Fund assets of approximately £4.5 billion at 31 March 2026, compared with £4.1 billion the previous year.
findings.detail: The auditor records the Fund as being in a strong financial position. The 2025 triennial valuation was completed and the Funding Strategy Statement was published in March 2026.
findings.matters: Pension fund assets and the triennial valuation outcome are the figures LGPS administering authorities and their peers compare.
findings.quote: assets of approximately £4.5 billion at 31 March 2026, compared with £4.1 billion in the previous year

findings.paper_title: Appendix 9 - Auditor’s Annual Report year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: ERP programme delayed since the year end, with a revised implementation date being agreed.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council is currently working to agree a revised implementation date. The auditor will review progress as part of its 2026/27 value-for-money work.
findings.matters: A delayed ERP programme affects the finance systems a council relies on, which is a point other finance teams weighing similar projects will consider.
findings.quote: Since the year end, the Council's ERP programme has been delayed

findings.paper_title: Appendix 9 - Auditor’s Annual Report year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Key recommendation on contract management: Internal Audit found supplier overcharges and weaknesses in contract monitoring.
findings.detail: The auditor retains the procurement and commissioning significant weakness and raises a new key recommendation for a review of governance and contract management in 2026/27. The paper also records that the ERP programme has been delayed since the year end.
findings.matters: A key recommendation on contract management across the whole organisation, not just individual services, is a point other councils will test against their own contract oversight.
findings.quote: The reviews highlighted issues including supplier overcharges

findings.paper_title: Appendix 9 - Auditor’s Annual Report year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Annual Governance Statement published in August 2026, after the 30 June 2026 statutory deadline.
findings.detail: The draft Statement of Accounts did not include the AGS, as required by the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015. The auditor records this as part of its improvement recommendation on legislative compliance.
findings.matters: A missed statutory deadline on the AGS is a compliance point other councils will check in their own closedown.
findings.quote: The AGS was subsequently published in August 2026, after the statutory deadline of 30 June 2026
